J.criterion: 语义闭合：单次求值、赋值、链续、多次、链尾、无 ?.、无 own
J.summary: The single-hop lowering works on the existing emitter (assignment form byte-identical to the split RHS), and chain-tail/multiple/own/?./static exclusions are implementable with existing flags or with parser rejection that already exists. But A is unimplemented, and two semantic boundaries are not closed: (a) assignment RHS with a side-effectful LHS (`a[i++] = chain$...`) is moved before the LHS, contradicting 'the prefix is the first evaluated part' (the existing hoist shares the assumption, but A does not exclude the shape); (b) a `for`-init declaration is claimed as a non-static local declaration initializer, but its emitter path is the for-header hoist, not the statement prelude. gaps: No A prototype: every semantic claim is a design inference, not an executed result.
Assignment LHS evaluation order is not addressed; a side-effectful LHS can observe a different order than the single-line expression.
`for`-init declaration context is not separated from statement-level preludes.
Multi-materialize overwrite of boxed values can leak (see J-4).

J.criterion: 类型闭合：已声明/已初始化、返回类型匹配、--types 负例、无推断
J.summary: The same-unit trait/interface class is feasible: --types already catches `int bad = i.next()` as `initializer: expected 'int', got 'struct M_iface'`, and generic inherent returns have inst_method_ret. But A explicitly allows type-host methods (`map ... for type`) and its main example uses one, and that class fails the stated --types requirement. At baseline `ct check --types` rejects any import outright; at v0.68.0 it accepts imports but exits 0 for `int bad = "...".method("GET")`, so the mismatch only becomes a C compiler error in build mode. `static_ctype` also has no aux==6 branch, so the `$` parser path cannot type the host result without new code. 'Initialized' is only a syntactic marker: it rejects the legal `M j; j = i.next();` and accepts `int x = y;` with uninitialized y.
J.scope: Fail is for the criterion as written, which includes the host-method class. Restricting A to same-unit trait/interface methods would move this to largely-pass; extending --types/build-mode checking or adding the static_ctype aux6 branch is the missing work.
gaps: No `$`-position type check exists, so the negative case cannot be executed.
Syntactic init is unsound for `T x = y;` and over-strict for flow-init.

J.criterion: 语法闭合：$ 第 4 义项与 range/into/errdefer/标识符的边界；lexer/parser 分支

The parser has exactly one primary `$` branch (into/range) and no postfix `$` branch, so `$NAME` is a clean new postfix branch rather than an ambiguity. Existing flags separate the three current meanings: into_node>=0, range_ctx=1 (only range elements), dollar_ok=1 && range_ctx=0 (trailing/defer). `?.m()` is already rejected; static calls are N_MCALL with a=-1/aux=11 and free calls are N_CALL, so the new branch can require a receiver-bearing method call. No parser prototype was built, so the branch is validated only by code inspection and boundary probes.

J.criterion: 所有权/生命周期：接口值/结构体/指针赋值，是否复制/悬挂；不自动释放
J.summary: The lowering is ordinary assignment: interface fat pointers copy (self+vt, no deep copy), structs copy by value, boxed returns copy the box pointer; no free is emitted, so there is no new auto-release and no new dangling. key_findings: The baseline label is wrong: 0c449d2e is v0.65.1 (32 commits after tag v0.65.1), not v0.67.0. The claim/counter version note is correct.
A's single-hop lowering is real: `j = i.next(); j.val()` emits exactly the assignment form of the split C (assignment RHS byte-identical to the declaration split).
A's 'initialized' predicate is syntactic only: it rejects `M j; j = i.next();` (common, legal) and accepts `int x = y;` with uninitialized y.

The host-method class defeats J-2's --types requirement: baseline --types rejects imports; v0.68.0 accepts them but silently returns 0 for a wrong-type host call, leaving the error to cc. static_ctype also lacks the aux==6 branch (claim C5).
SH-73 is not fixed: the reject is unchanged and --types is blind to it; the split/variable-receiver bypass works, and A is that bypass in one line.
B's two-line equivalence is position-limited: `c && chain` / `c ? chain : 0` print 0 0 one-line vs 0 2 split. into cannot change type and rejects interface/own.

Cost: 6-8 source files is defensible (four duplicated node-kind units + Symbols + grammar); 150-250 source lines is optimistic (~180-320 structural estimate); docs/tests are understated. Zero `$NAME` sites make old goldens/revert clean.
limitations: A is a proposal, not an implementation: no parser/emitter/type-check prototype was built in this seat (the battle forbids touching selfhost/** beyond /tmp copies). All A-behaviour statements are design inferences plus emitted-C equivalence for the manual lowering.
No ASan/ownership matrix was run; the J-4 answer is based on generated C (no free, fat-pointer copy) and the own-reassignment probe.
HEAD was moving during the session (v0.68.0 -> v0.68.0-4); all baseline evidence is pinned to the immutable 0c449d2e snapshot. The v0.68.0 cross-check is labelled separately.

The question's `HttpRequest req = init(); "...".method("GET")$req...` mixes a type-host first hop with a trait interface; in the current unit matrix the type-host result is a concrete `struct HttpRequest`, and a same-named trait is shadowed (E18). This does not affect the lowering mechanics but affects which class of site A actually serves.
verdict_note: No final A/B verdict is written by VERIFY. The J-1..J-6 statuses are evidence judgments: J-2 fail is scoped to the host-method/--types class; J-1/J-6 are unresolved without a prototype; J-3/J-4/J-5 pass on the executed/inspected evidence with the stated gaps.
